pages.title: Read the situation

pages.author: Scenario briefing · fictional
pages.subject: Whose bag is this?
paragraphs: Lost-property example: open backpack, charger, boarding pass with no readable date, black notebook with a silver star, red fish key ring. Do not read personal document details or infer the owner’s nationality or job. Reception handles collection.

pages.title: Practise the conversation
pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Someone has left a backpack by our table. Should we take it to reception?
lines.audioText: Someone has left a backpack by our table. Should we take it to reception?
lines.translation: Alguém deixou uma mochila perto da mesa. Devemos levá-la à recepção?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Yes. There’s a boarding pass visible in the open pocket. The owner might be travelling
lines.audioText: Yes. There’s a boarding pass visible in the open pocket. The owner might be travelling.
lines.translation: Sim. Tem um cartão de embarque visível no bolso aberto. A pessoa pode estar viajando

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Maybe, but it could be an old pass. We don’t know the date
lines.audioText: Maybe, but it could be an old pass. We don’t know the date.
lines.translation: Talvez, mas pode ser antigo. Não sabemos a data

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: True. There’s also a charger and a black notebook
lines.audioText: True. There’s also a charger and a black notebook.
lines.translation: Verdade. Também tem um carregador e um caderno preto

questions.answer: The backpack was left by their table

questions.prompt: Why might the owner be travelling?
questions.answer: There is a boarding pass visible in the open pocket

questions.prompt: Does the boarding pass prove the owner is travelling today?
questions.answer: No, the pass could be old and they don’t know its date

pages.title: Practise the conversation
pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Those are common things. What detail could help reception identify it?
lines.audioText: Those are common things. What detail could help reception identify it?
lines.translation: São coisas comuns. Que detalhe ajudaria a recepção a identificar?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: The notebook has a silver star, and the key ring is a red fish
lines.audioText: The notebook has a silver star, and the key ring is a red fish.
lines.translation: O caderno tem uma estrela prateada e o chaveiro é um peixe vermelho

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: That’s more useful. Let’s let the caller describe those before we suggest them
lines.audioText: That’s more useful. Let’s let the caller describe those before we suggest them.
lines.translation: Isso ajuda mais. Vamos deixar quem ligar descrever antes de sugerirmos

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Agreed. We can make a guess, but we shouldn’t hand it over without checking
lines.audioText: Agreed. We can make a guess, but we shouldn’t hand it over without checking.
lines.translation: Concordo. Podemos levantar uma hipótese, mas não entregar sem conferir

pages.title: Listen and answer
pages.instruction: A caller gives matching details. Listen for the new information and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana. Reception has spoken to a caller about the backpack. The caller described a black notebook with a silver star and a red fish key ring, without being told those details first. Both descriptions match the objects in our example. That makes the claim more plausible, but reception still needs to follow its collection procedure. Could you explain why the matching details are stronger evidence than simply having a charger, and say what still needs to be checked?
pages.audioText: Hi, Ana. Reception has spoken to a caller about the backpack. The caller described a black notebook with a silver star and a red fish key ring, without being told those details first. Both descriptions match the objects in our example. That makes the claim more plausible, but reception still needs to follow its collection procedure. Could you explain why the matching details are stronger evidence than simply having a charger, and say what still needs to be checked?
pages.greeting: Someone has called about the backpack

items.prompt: What did the caller correctly describe?

items.prompt: Why are those details stronger evidence than a charger?

items.prompt: What still needs to happen before collection?
items.answer: Reception still needs to follow its collection procedure
